passages.text: “Call out if you please, but who will answer? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
passages.sermon:
A man may call out for help.
No one may answer him.
He may look for someone holy to help him.
He will not find anyone to turn to.
passages.original: קְֽרָא־ נָ֭א הֲיֵ֣שׁ עוֹנֶ֑ךָּ וְאֶל־ מִ֖י מִקְּדֹשִׁ֣ים תִּפְנֶֽה׃

passages.text: For resentment kills a fool, and envy slays the simple.
passages.sermon:
A fool is a person who rejects wisdom.
Resentment destroys a fool.
A simple person lacks understanding.
Envy kills the simple person.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ לֶֽ֭אֱוִיל יַהֲרָג־ כָּ֑עַשׂ וּ֝פֹתֶ֗ה תָּמִ֥ית קִנְאָֽה׃

passages.text: I have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly his house was cursed.
passages.sermon:
A fool is a person who rejects wisdom.
I have seen a fool begin to grow strong.
He seemed to become established.
But suddenly, his house was cursed.
His security did not last.
passages.original: אֲ‍ֽנִי־ רָ֭אִיתִי אֱוִ֣יל מַשְׁרִ֑ישׁ וָאֶקּ֖וֹב נָוֵ֣הוּ פִתְאֹֽם׃

passages.text: His sons are far from safety, crushed in court without a defender.
passages.sermon:
A fool’s sons are in danger.
They are far from safety.
People crush them at the city gate.
No one defends them.
No one saves them.
passages.original: יִרְחֲק֣וּ בָנָ֣יו מִיֶּ֑שַׁע וְיִֽדַּכְּא֥וּ בַ֝שַּׁ֗עַר וְאֵ֣ין מַצִּֽיל׃

passages.text: The hungry consume his harvest, taking it even from the thorns, and the thirsty pant after his wealth.
passages.sermon: The hungry eat his harvest.\r\nThey take his harvest even from among the thorns.\r\nThe thirsty long for his wealth.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֤ר קְצִיר֨וֹ׀ רָ֘עֵ֤ב יֹאכֵ֗ל וְאֶֽל־ מִצִּנִּ֥ים יִקָּחֵ֑הוּ וְשָׁאַ֖ף צַמִּ֣ים חֵילָֽם׃

passages.text: For distress does not spring from the dust, and trouble does not sprout from the ground.
passages.sermon: Distress does not come from the dust.\r\nTrouble does not grow out of the ground.\r\nThese things do not appear by themselves from the earth.
passages.original: כִּ֤י׀ לֹא־ יֵצֵ֣א מֵעָפָ֣ר אָ֑וֶן וּ֝מֵאֲדָמָ֗ה לֹא־ יִצְמַ֥ח עָמָֽל׃

passages.text: Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
passages.sermon:
Man is born for trouble.
Trouble comes to every person.
Sparks always fly upward.
In the same way, trouble rises up in human life.
This happens to all people.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אָ֭דָם לְעָמָ֣ל יוּלָּ֑ד וּבְנֵי־ רֶ֝֗שֶׁף יַגְבִּ֥יהוּ עֽוּף׃

passages.text: However, if I were you, I would appeal to God and lay my cause before Him— the One who does great and unsearchable things, wonders without number.
passages.sermon:
God does great things.
No one can fully understand His works.
He performs wonders.
No one can count all His wonders.
If I were you, I would turn to God.
I would bring my case to Him.
passages.original: אוּלָ֗ם אֲ֭נִי אֶדְרֹ֣שׁ אֶל־ אֵ֑ל וְאֶל־ אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים אָשִׂ֥ים דִּבְרָתִֽי׃ עֹשֶׂ֣ה גְ֭דֹלוֹת וְאֵ֣ין חֵ֑קֶר נִ֝פְלָא֗וֹת עַד־ אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃

passages.text: He gives rain to the earth and sends water upon the fields.
passages.sermon: God gives rain to the earth.\r\nGod sends water on the fields.
passages.original: הַנֹּתֵ֣ן מָ֭טָר עַל־ פְּנֵי־ אָ֑רֶץ וְשֹׁ֥לֵֽחַ מַ֝יִם עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י חוּצֽוֹת׃

passages.text: He sets the lowly on high, so that mourners are lifted to safety.
passages.sermon:
God acts with great power.
God lifts up people who are lowly.
God raises humble people to a high place.
God helps those who mourn.
God brings mourners to a place of safety.
passages.original: לָשׂ֣וּם שְׁפָלִ֣ים לְמָר֑וֹם וְ֝קֹדְרִ֗ים שָׂ֣גְבוּ יֶֽשַׁע׃

passages.text: He thwarts the schemes of the crafty, so that their hands find no success.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power and wisdom.
God stops the plans of crafty people.
God makes sure their hands do not succeed.
God does not let their efforts bring success.
passages.original: מֵ֭פֵר מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת עֲרוּמִ֑ים וְֽלֹא־ תַעֲשֶׂ֥ינָה יְ֝דֵיהֶ֗ם תּוּשִׁיָּֽה׃

passages.text: He catches the wise in their craftiness, and sweeps away the plans of the cunning.
passages.sermon: God acts with power and wisdom.\r\nGod catches wise people when they act with craftiness.\r\nGod destroys the plans of cunning people quickly.
passages.original: לֹכֵ֣ד חֲכָמִ֣ים בְּעָרְמָ֑ם וַעֲצַ֖ת נִפְתָּלִ֣ים נִמְהָֽרָה׃

passages.text: They encounter darkness by day and grope at noon as in the night.
passages.sermon:
God judges the wicked and the cunning.
They meet darkness during the day.
At noon, they grope as if it were night.
They cannot find their way, even when the sun shines.
God confuses their plans and actions.
passages.original: יוֹמָ֥ם יְפַגְּשׁוּ־ חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וְ֝כַלַּ֗יְלָה יְֽמַשְׁשׁ֥וּ בַֽצָּהֳרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: He saves the needy from the sword in their mouth and from the clutches of the powerful.
passages.sermon: God saves the needy.\r\nHe rescues them from the sword that comes from the mouths of their enemies.\r\nHe delivers the needy from the hands of the powerful.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣שַׁע מֵ֭חֶרֶב מִפִּיהֶ֑ם וּמִיַּ֖ד חָזָ֣ק אֶבְיֽוֹן׃

passages.text: So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.
passages.sermon:
God cares for the poor.
The poor have hope because of God.
Injustice cannot speak against them.
Injustice closes its mouth.
passages.original: וַתְּהִ֣י לַדַּ֣ל תִּקְוָ֑ה וְ֝עֹלָ֗תָה קָ֣פְצָה פִּֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Blessed indeed is the man whom God corrects; so do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.
passages.sermon:
God corrects people.
A person is blessed when God corrects him.
The Almighty gives discipline.
Do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֤ה אַשְׁרֵ֣י אֱ֭נוֹשׁ יוֹכִחֶ֣נּֽוּ אֱל֑וֹהַּ וּמוּסַ֥ר שַׁ֝דַּ֗י אַל־ תִּמְאָֽס׃

passages.text: For He wounds, but He also binds; He strikes, but His hands also heal.
passages.sermon:
God is powerful.
God sometimes causes pain.
God also brings healing.
God may strike a person.
God’s hands can restore and heal that person.
passages.original: כִּ֤י ה֣וּא יַכְאִ֣יב וְיֶחְבָּ֑שׁ יִ֝מְחַ֗ץ וְיָדוֹ תִּרְפֶּֽינָה׃

passages.text: He will rescue you from six calamities; no harm will touch you in seven.
passages.sermon:
God is powerful and cares for people.
God will rescue you from six troubles.
No harm will touch you in seven troubles.
God protects you in every danger.
God keeps you safe from harm.
passages.original: בְּשֵׁ֣שׁ צָ֭רוֹת יַצִּילֶ֑ךָּ וּבְשֶׁ֓בַע׀ לֹא־ יִגַּ֖ע בְּךָ֣ רָֽע׃

passages.text: In famine He will redeem you from death, and in battle from the stroke of the sword.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power and mercy.
God saves His people.
God redeems you from death during famine.
God rescues you from the sword during battle.
passages.original: בְּ֭רָעָב פָּֽדְךָ֣ מִמָּ֑וֶת וּ֝בְמִלְחָמָ֗ה מִ֣ידֵי חָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, and will not fear havoc when it comes.
passages.sermon:
God protects you from harmful words.
You will not suffer when people speak against you.
You will not be afraid when disaster comes.
You will remain safe even when trouble arrives.
passages.original: בְּשׁ֣וֹט לָ֭שׁוֹן תֵּחָבֵ֑א וְֽלֹא־ תִירָ֥א מִ֝שֹּׁ֗ד כִּ֣י יָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: You will laugh at destruction and famine, and need not fear the beasts of the earth.
passages.sermon:
God protects the righteous.
You will see destruction.
You will see famine.
You will laugh at both destruction and famine.
You will not fear wild animals on the earth.
God keeps you safe from harm.
passages.original: לְשֹׁ֣ד וּלְכָפָ֣ן תִּשְׂחָ֑ק וּֽמֵחַיַּ֥ת הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ אַל־ תִּירָֽא׃

passages.text: For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you.
passages.sermon:
God will protect you.
You will have a covenant with the stones of the field.
The wild animals will be at peace with you.
You will not face harm from nature.
God will keep you safe in the land.
passages.original: כִּ֤י עִם־ אַבְנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֣ה בְרִיתֶ֑ךָ וְחַיַּ֥ת הַ֝שָּׂדֶ֗ה הָשְׁלְמָה־ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: You will know that your tent is secure, and find nothing amiss when inspecting your home.
passages.sermon: You will know that your home is safe.\r\nYou will check your dwelling.\r\nYou will find nothing wrong.
passages.original: וְֽ֭יָדַעְתָּ כִּי־ שָׁל֣וֹם אָהֳלֶ֑ךָ וּֽפָקַדְתָּ֥ נָ֝וְךָ וְלֹ֣א תֶחֱטָֽא׃

passages.text: You will know that your offspring will be many, your descendants like the grass of the earth.
passages.sermon:
You will know this truth.
You will have many children.
Your descendants will be very numerous.
They will be as many as the grass on the earth.
passages.original: וְֽ֭יָדַעְתָּ כִּי־ רַ֣ב זַרְעֶ֑ךָ וְ֝צֶאֱצָאֶ֗יךָ כְּעֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: You will come to the grave in full vigor, like a sheaf of grain gathered in season.
passages.sermon:
This passage speaks about a righteous person.
A righteous person will reach old age with strength.
You will come to the grave in full vigor.
You will be like a sheaf of grain.
Workers gather a sheaf of grain at the right time.
You will reach the end of your life at the proper time.
You will be strong and complete when your life ends.
passages.original: תָּב֣וֹא בְכֶ֣לַח אֱלֵי־ קָ֑בֶר כַּעֲל֖וֹת גָּדִ֣ישׁ בְּעִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Indeed, we have investigated, and it is true! So hear it and know for yourself.”
passages.sermon:
We have carefully examined this matter.
We know it is true.
Listen to what we say.
Understand this for yourself.
passages.original: הִנֵּה־ זֹ֭את חֲקַרְנ֥וּהָ כֶּֽן־ הִ֑יא שְׁ֝מָעֶ֗נָּה וְאַתָּ֥ה דַֽע־ לָֽךְ׃פ
